drhp.business: PTL Enterprises owns a tyre manufacturing facility that it has leased out to Apollo Tyres Ltd. (ATL); the Company itself carries out no manufacturing operations of its own and its income is derived from lease rent of the tyre unit. The truck-bus cross-ply tyres manufactured at the Company's leased plant are made under the 'Apollo' brand and are mostly sold or exported by Apollo Tyres Ltd. Because the facility is leased out, cost audit and the energy/technology-absorption disclosures are not applicable to the Company.

risks.note: The MD&A SWOT lists 'Dependence on ATL' as a Weakness. The Company's tyre facility is leased to Apollo Tyres Ltd. and, per the Directors' Report, the Company 'does not have its own production as its facility has been leased out to Apollo Tyres Ltd.' - so effectively the entire operating income stream rests on one counterparty.
risks.risk: Single-lessee dependence on Apollo Tyres Ltd.

risks.note: Stated verbatim as a Weakness: 'Any impact on margins and revenue of ATL might force ATL to renegotiate the Lease Agreement.' Because the Company's income is fixed lease rent, a renegotiation would reset its earnings base directly.
risks.risk: Lease renegotiation risk if the lessee's economics deteriorate

risks.note: Listed as a Weakness in the MD&A SWOT. The Company has no operating business, no manufacturing of its own, and therefore no independent lever on volumes, pricing or mix; energy/technology-absorption and cost-audit requirements are 'not applicable' precisely because it does not manufacture.
risks.risk: No direct presence in the tyre market

risks.note: Stated as a Threat: 'Economic downturn or slowdown in the key markets of ATL (India and Europe) can lead to decreased volumes and capacity utilisation by the leasee.' Lower utilisation of the leased plant weakens the lessee's willingness to sustain lease terms.
risks.risk: Demand cyclicality in the lessee's key markets (India and Europe)

risks.note: Stated as a Threat: 'Continuing high inflation and raw material cost escalation will add to pressure on margins of ATL.' Margin pressure at the lessee is the trigger the SWOT itself links to lease renegotiation.
risks.risk: Raw-material cost escalation and inflation compressing the lessee's margins

risks.note: Stated as a Threat: 'A weak Indian currency can result in pressure on margins of the ATL, since the ATL is a net importer.' The Company itself reported no foreign exchange earnings or outgo during the year, so the exposure is indirect but real through the lease counterparty.
risks.risk: Currency risk transmitted through the lessee

risks.note: The MD&A Outlook flags that the outlook 'continues to be influenced by external factors, including trade policy shifts, energy price volatility and geopolitical developments across key regions', which 'may impact supply chains, inflation trajectories and overall demand conditions across markets' - all of which feed the lessee's volumes and, in turn, the lease.

The Ind AS 24 note shows Apollo Tyres Ltd. - an enterprise owned or significantly influenced by KMP - as the counterparty for income from lease/services, reimbursement of expenses, rent paid and services received, with outstanding balances at year end. Revenue concentration in a single related party makes lease pricing a governance as well as a commercial exposure.
risks.risk: Related-party concentration in the income stream
